description: Search US federal PROCUREMENT CONTRACTS / government contract awards for goods and services. Use recipient_name for "contracts won by Lockheed Martin"; keywords searches award descriptions/topics, not contractor identity. Dates are optional and default to the last 12 months for "recent" questions. Dates select awards ACTIVE in the window (not signed in it) and award_amount is the award's LIFETIME obligation, so do not sum it as spending for the period. Results are paged: 100 per page max — pass `page` (and read `page_metadata.has_next`) to reach the rest. Returns recipient, award amount, outlays (with an outlays_reported flag, since DoD awards usually report none), dates, and contract type. Umbrella contracts (IDVs — CRS-2, NASA Launch Services II, CCtCap) are a SEPARATE result set in `idvs`, not in `awards`: read both, and `idv_status` says which you got. IDV and child-order amounts are disjoint, so `totals.combined_amount` is the correct total.

agency.description: Awarding agency — full toptier name ("Department of Defense") or the common abbreviation (DOD, DHS, VA, HHS, DOE, NASA, GSA, USDA, EPA…), which is expanded for you.

include_idvs.description: Include umbrella contracts (indefinite delivery vehicles) as a separate `idvs` array. Default true. Leave it on: these are often a recipient's largest awards, and excluding them understates a total silently.

limit.description: Number of results per page (1-100, default 10)

page.description: 1-based page number (default 1). total_results can exceed limit; page through with this and read page_metadata.has_next / total_pages to reach every row. The `idvs` array is served on page 1 only.

recipient_name.description: Contractor/recipient name (e.g., "Lockheed Martin"). Use for awards won by a company; do not put company names in keywords. Matched as a SUBSTRING of the registered legal name, so a brand name can miss the company entirely ("SpaceX" is not inside "SPACE EXPLORATION TECHNOLOGIES CORP."); a known brand that matches nothing is retried under its legal name and the response says so in `recipient_resolution`. An empty result distinguishes `no_match` (no registered recipient has this name) from `recipient_matched_no_awards` (it does, but holds nothing under your window/agency filters) and lists the near-miss names in `recipient_candidates`.

set_aside.description: Small-business set-aside filter. Accepts a family name ("HUBZone", "8(a)", "WOSB", "EDWOSB", "SDVOSB", "Veteran", "Small business", "Indian"), a FAR code ("HZC", "8AN", "SDVOSBC"), or the literal USAspending description ("HUBZONE SET-ASIDE"). Matches both the set-aside and sole-source variants of a family.

state.description: Place-of-performance US state, 2-letter code (e.g., "MD", "TX"). Filters to contracts performed in that state.

name: usa_award_search
